**Opportunity Data Call \- ONR Code 08 IT Support Services**

***Instructions*** 

| *VOLUME IV: TECHNICAL DEMONSTRATION CONTENT (FACTOR 3\)*    *11.1 Purpose: The purpose of the Pre-Recorded Technical Demonstration is to allow the Government to evaluate the functionality, agility, security, usability, and future-readiness of the Offeror's proposed Data and Analytics solution, and to assess the hands-on technical competence of their proposed Key Personnel. Volume IV must contain the submission link and supporting access documentation for the technical demonstration.  11.2 Technical Demonstration Details & Logistics:  (a) Secure Link Submission: Provide a single page containing a secure, private, password-protected URL link, such as Vimeo or YouTube, to the pre-recorded technical demonstration video. Provide all necessary login credentials.  (b) Duration: The total video recording shall not exceed fifty (50) minutes. Offerors must sequentially execute the prescribed scenario elements and address the strategic prompts within this uninterrupted timeframe.  (c) Environment & Format: The demonstration must showcase a live, functioning cloud environment representative of the proposed solution (configured for security baseline equivalents) and live code repositories. The use of static slide decks (e.g.,  Microsoft PowerPoint) is strictly prohibited. Highly edited screen captures, post-production marketing overlays, or simulated application videos will result in an "Unacceptable" rating for this factor.  (d) Data Constraints: The Offeror shall use sanitized, open-source, or mock data representing typical command datasets (e.g., mock S\&T project registries, financial ERP sheets). Under no circumstances shall actual Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), personally identifiable information (PII), or classified data be uploaded to or demonstrated within the environment.  (e) Presenters: The demonstration and narration must be led primarily by the Offeror's proposed Key Personnel (e.g., Chief Enterprise Architect, DevSecOps Engineer, Data Scientist). Corporate business development, sales, or non-technical account representatives may facilitate introductions but are strictly prohibited from leading, demonstrating, or narrating technical elements.  ![][image1] ![A close-up of a white backgroundDescription automatically generated][image2]* 7.0 EVALUATION OF FACTOR 3: TECHNICAL DEMONSTRATION, VOLUME IV Factor 3 is the sole rated non-price factor and will receive an adjectival rating, which can be Outstanding, Good, Acceptable, Marginal, or Unacceptable. For Sub-Factor 3.1, a proposal that merely meets the baseline requirements will be rated as "Acceptable." Higher ratings, such as Good or Outstanding, may be assigned to proposals that offer strengths or significant strengths within the Pre-Recorded Technical Demonstration:	 (1) A strength is an aspect of the proposal that exceeds a requirement in a way that is advantageous to the Government. (2) A significant strength is an aspect of the proposal that appreciably increases the likelihood of successful contract performance, provides exceptional benefit, or greatly reduces risk.					 Sub-Factor 3.1: Pre-Recorded Technical Demonstration The Government will evaluate the Pre-Recorded Technical Demonstration on an adjectival scale based on the following criteria:						 (1) Technical Competence (Key Personnel): The extent to which the proposed Key Personnel demonstrated expert-level, hands-on understanding of the platform's underlying architecture, code bases, and workflows in the video without relying on corporate back-office support.						 (2) Completeness of Scenario Execution: Successful, seamless execution of all seven (7) scenario elements and adequate response to all five (5) strategic prompts within the allotted 50-minute window.				 (3) Open Architecture and Non-Proprietary Standards: Evidence that the system uses modular, loosely coupled design patterns, standard APIs, and portable data storage models to prevent vendor lock-in and enable interoperability with DOW/DON platforms. (4) Strategic Alignment and Agility: The capability of the platform and the team to rapidly adapt to changing command strategies, evolving technology fields, and workforce automation needs as demonstrated during the scenario execution and narrated strategic prompt responses.   |

**11.3 Demonstration Scenario Elements:**   
The Offeror must sequentially execute and explain all seven (7) of the following elements to prove their capability to execute the [Performance Work Statement (PWS)](https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1JeKkll06kKXaQQ730RDlTr0CRmVvpdBu):   
**Element 1: Secure Access, Authentication, and Zero Trust**  
**(a) Action:** Demonstrate a user authenticating and accessing the platform's portal interface.

**(b) Focus:** Explicitly showcase the integration of Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) and explain how the identity provider and access controls align with DoD Zero Trust Architecture principles (least-privilege access, continuous authorization, etc.). 

***(c) Zero Trust & Cybersecurity Compliance (IL4/IL5 Baseline):** Detail how the proposed application architecture implements micro-segmentation, continuous compliance, and least-privilege boundary configurations within a DoD Impact Level 5 (IL5) hosting environment.* 

**Element 2: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and Automation**  
**(a) Action:** Provide a live visual walk-through (via command line, cloud console, or repository) of how the demonstration environment was provisioned and configured.

**(b) Focus:** Demonstrate the use of IaC and configuration management utilities (e.g., Terraform, Ansible, or equivalent) and CI/CD deployment pipelines, showing how configurations are version-controlled and deployed securely. 

**Element 3: Automated Ingestion, Data Operations, and Streaming**  
**(a) Action:** Ingest a raw, unstructured, or semi-structured sample dataset (such as a mock registry of research grants) into the platform.

**(b) Focus:** Demonstrate how automated ingestion pipelines (ETL/ELT) detect incoming files, run automated quality checks, and handle schema variations. Explain or demonstrate how the architecture supports near-real-time data streaming (e.g., Kafka, Kinesis, or equivalent). 

**Element 4: Data Governance, Quality, and Cataloging**  
**(a) Action:** Navigate to the platform's data management registry, catalog, or dictionary interface.

**(b) Focus:** Demonstrate how the ingested dataset is cataloged, how metadata is captured, and how the platform calculates data quality or health scores. Show how end-to-end data lineage is visually mapped from raw ingestion to the visualization tier. 

**Element 5: Decision-Support Analytics and Modeling**  
**(a) Action:** Trigger and execute an analytical routine or statistical/machine learning model against the ingested sample dataset. 

(b) Focus: Show how the model outputs (e.g., forecasting, predictive velocities, trend IDs) are generated and structured. Demonstrate how these analytics serve as strategic decision-making aids for leadership. 

**Element 6: Unified Dashboard, Visualizations, and Process Automation**  
**(a) Action:** Access the graphical user interface (UI) or embedded executive business intelligence (BI) dashboard.

**(b) Focus:** Demonstrate how a non-technical leader can search, filter, and extract insights. Show how the platform automates repetitive workflows (e.g., automated summaries, approval routings, anomaly flagging) to drive efficiency. 

**Element 7: Interoperability, Data Portability, and Secure Export**  
**(a) Action:** Execute a secure, bulk data export or extraction of a filtered dataset.

**(b) Focus:** Prove compliance with open data standards by exporting information in a non-proprietary format (e.g., CSV, JSON, Parquet). Explain how the schemas and APIs support seamless integration with broader enterprise cloud platforms (such as Advana or Cloud One) to prevent vendor lock-in. 

***11.4 Strategic Prompts (Narrated Address):***   
*Because there is no live Q\&A session, the Offeror's Key Personnel must verbally address the following five (5) mandatory strategic prompts during the recording. Offerors may narrate these answers while executing the scenario elements or as a dedicated speaking segment within the video:* 

**(a) Sustainment of the Legacy Footprint:** Detail your exact technical approach for sustaining and operating the current legacy D\&A Portal application, reporting systems, databases, and existing ETL pipelines, ensuring zero service degradation or operational gaps during modernization phases. 

**(b) Financial & Budgetary Analytical Integration:** Describe how your platform's analytical modeling techniques (predictive, prescriptive) and your proposed team will support financial execution tracking, budget formulation, and cost optimization for various command resourcing priorities. 

**(c) Zero Trust & Cybersecurity Compliance (IL4/IL5 Baseline):** Detail how the proposed application architecture implements micro-segmentation, continuous compliance, and least-privilege boundary configurations within a DoD Impact Level 5 (IL5) hosting environment. 

**(d) Disaster Recovery, Resilience, and Failover:** Explain your approach to business continuity, specifically detailing: Target Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO); High-availability cloud configuration patterns; and your strategy for conducting non-disruptive annual disaster recovery exercises. 

**(e) Data Vendor and Lifecycle Management:** Explain your methodology and tooling for tracking commercial data subscriptions, monitoring data-usage licenses, validating data quality compliance, and managing renewals without causing data gaps in critical analytical dashboards.
